summary.text: Tim Walberg is the U.S. Representative for Michigan's 5th District, which he has represented since redistricting took effect in 2023, and won re-election on November 3, 2026.

A minister and Moody Bible Institute manager who served 16 years in the Michigan House, he first took office in Congress in 2007, representing Michigan's 7th District from 2007 to 2009 and again from 2011 to 2023.
He chairs the House Committee on Education and the Workforce.

paragraphs.text: Tim Walberg was born in Chicago, Illinois, in 1951. He attended Moody Bible Institute and earned a bachelor's degree from Fort Wayne Bible College in 1975 and a master's degree from Wheaton College in 1978.

According to his House website, he served as a pastor in Michigan and Indiana, as president of the Warren Reuther Center for Education and Community Impact, and as a division manager for Moody Bible Institute before entering public office.
Walberg served in the Michigan House of Representatives from 1983 to 1999.
He took office in the U.S. House in 2007 representing Michigan's 7th District, succeeding Joe Schwarz, and served until 2009, when Mark Schauer succeeded him in the seat.

He returned to the U.S. House in 2011 for the 7th District and, after redistricting, has represented the 5th District since 2023. His House website calls him the dean of the Michigan congressional delegation and says he is serving his ninth term.
In the 119th Congress Walberg chairs the House Committee on Education and the Workforce and also serves on the Natural Resources Committee.

His House website says the Center for Effective Lawmaking, a Vanderbilt University and University of Virginia collaboration, ranked him the most effective member of Michigan's congressional delegation in the 115th Congress, and it cites his American Conservative Union lifetime score.
According to his House website, he and his wife, Sue, have been married for more than 50 years, have three children and seven grandchildren, and live in Tipton, Michigan.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 59.1% of the vote to Christian Vukasovich's 38.6%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
